numbering_policy: Original Saints references, chapters, reading sections, anchors and continuation bodies are preserved. Missing original verse numbers are not filled from another edition.
review_notes: Read all 73 actual source units in Mark 1–2 from the exact pinned Saints English record, after the parent confirmed that every original Matthew source unit had been read.

Every retained target was read in the exact Saints originals with the surrounding narrative or discourse where needed. Original target ordering, absent-verse gaps and Greek-based book divisions remain intact.

The opening composite citation is handled without silently changing Mark's Isaiah attribution: the messenger clause is compared with Malachi 3:1 and Exodus 23:20, and the wilderness-voice clause with Isaiah 40:3.

Mark's Spirit descending into Him and Matthew's upon Him are kept distinct. Luke's fire in John's baptism saying is not added to Mark, and Mark's wild animals are not inserted into the other wilderness accounts.

The searching groups in Mark and Luke, the healing-summary quantities, the Levi call details, pronouns in the meal complaint and the tile-versus-dug-roof descriptions are qualified rather than harmonized.

The bread episode preserves Mark's Abiathar and the Saints Samuel record's Abimelech, without declaring the priest names identical or importing a different patronymic. Saints 1 Samuel 21:2–7 is used as saved.

A target range counts as one pair. Three sources have additional independently useful targets: Mark 1:2 for the composite wording, Mark 1:13 for angelic ministry alongside the testing setting, and Mark 2:26 for the original bread episode beside the Gospel parallel. Completion still counts each source only once.
The two deferred units receive zero completion credit. The hourly numerical target does not justify a generic connection.
No source wording, display wording, continuations, verse IDs or division membership is edited. This is an AI-assisted English initial passage review, with independent specialist review pending.

All76 actual Mark3–4 source units and every retained target passage were read from the exact Saints cache with surrounding context as needed. Matthew's entire original inventory had been read before Mark source review was authorized.

All74 paired sources have one retained proposal each. Two source units are explicitly deferred with zero completion credit. Source wording, IDs, chapter divisions, and continuation paragraphs are unchanged.

Boanerges/Sons of Thunder remains specific to Mark's list rather than being supplied to Matthew. The given apostolic names match Matthew's actual list; no Thaddaeus/Judas-son-of-James identity claim is needed or imposed.

The boat/crowd-pressure and inability-to-eat comparisons are qualified as different scenes or internal recurring patterns. The insanity accusation comparison does not make John's speakers the same people as Mark's own people.
Sower explanations, good-soil yield order, private explanation contexts, judgment/hearing applications of the measure saying, and lamp-saying locations are kept distinct where the Evangelists differ.

Joel's sickle comparison uses the actual Greek-based Saints reference Joel4:13 and preserves vintage/winepress language against Mark's grain harvest. No other edition's Joel3 numbering was substituted.
The naturally growing seed is not treated as the same parable as Matthew's hostile-darnel parable. The 1Corinthians comparison does not assert that Mark's verse explicitly names God as the grower.

Storm comparisons preserve different addresses, faith rebukes, and boat details without inventing a single wording for the accounts. These are AI-assisted English passage judgments, not independent human specialist or live-destination verification.

All 99 actual Mark 5–6 source units and every retained target passage were read from exact Saints cached snapshots. The 98 proposed completed sources have 98 pairs; Mark 5:5 remains deferred with zero completion credit.

Target IDs resolve, target passages follow contiguous original units, complete source coverage is exact, pair keys are unique, and no target contains its own source unit. Original words, gaps, and continuation structure were preserved.

Exorcism comparisons preserve country versus abyss, whole city versus Decapolis, two-thousand-pig count versus no count, and the difference between reports about the healed man and reports including pigs. No psychological diagnosis or manufactured event sequence is added.

Jairus comparisons distinguish Mark's initially dying daughter from Matthew's already-dead report. Aramaic Talitha koum is not inserted into Luke. Attendance restrictions distinguish accompanying Jesus from entering the room and the parents' participation.
The woman's medical history preserves Mark's worsening after suffering and Luke's no-cure formulation, without presenting the accounts as identical in every detail.

Hometown comparisons preserve carpenter versus craftsman's son, Joses versus Joseph, and could do no mighty work versus did not do many. Mission equipment preserves Mark's permitted staff and sandals versus Matthew's restrictions.
Mark 6:22's exact His daughter Herodias is retained beside Matthew's Herodias's daughter. No unverified identification as Salome or genealogical harmonization is supplied.

Herod's role remains distinct across accounts: Mark describes fear and protection of righteous John with glad but perplexed listening; Matthew describes wanting to kill John but fearing the crowd. Herodias's expressed desire and maternal prompting are not transferred between actors.

Feeding and water-walking comparisons preserve the accounts' withdrawal occasions, Bethsaida destination detail, grouping in hundreds and fifties, green grass, bread question, intention to pass by, Peter sequence, and differing descriptions of the disciples' reactions.
Mark 6:52 to 8:17–21 is explicitly a later same-book recurrence of hardheartedness and failure to understand the loaves, with an actual callback to five loaves, five thousand, and twelve baskets.

This is AI-assisted English passage review, not exhaustive concordance, fresh Greek critical-text or apparatus verification, independent human specialist approval, or live destination-anchor checking.
interpretation_scope: Connections are individually labelled; thematic or internal links do not establish identical events or independent testimony.
source_limitations: NA28 is the user-authorized provisional New Testament base. Focused checks of the German Bible Society’s Greek running text are recorded by chapter. This is an English editorial revision, not complete critical-text or apparatus verification. The newer Bespoke PDF’s preferred UBS6 text has not been obtained; UBS6/ECM comparison, full apparatus, independent Greek and human read-aloud reviews remain pending.
